statement: Let L_d be the list of values of all nodes at depth d in the tree, ordered from left to right (i.e., by a breadth-first traversal that visits left children before right children). The function returns a result r, and r is true if and only if for every integer d >= 0: if d is even, then every value in L_d is odd and for every i with 0 <= i < len(L_d) - 1, L_d[i] < L_d[i+1]; if d is odd, then every value in L_d is even and for every i with 0 <= i < len(L_d) - 1, L_d[i] > L_d[i+1]. (For levels beyond the height of the tree, L_d is empty and the conditions are vacuously true.)
preconditions: root is not Null; the tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes; every node value is an integer in [1, 10^6].

statement: The function returns a result r (i.e., it does not fail, panic, or overflow) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: root is not Null; the tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes; every node value is an integer in [1, 10^6].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r is true if and only if v0 is odd and v1 is even.
preconditions: root is a Node with value v0; exactly one of its children is a Node with value v1 and the other child is Null; that child v1 has both children Null (so the tree has exactly two nodes); v0 and v1 are integers in [1, 10^6].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r is true if and only if v0 is odd, v1 is even, v2 is even, and v1 > v2.
preconditions: root is a Node with value v0; both its left child (value v1) and right child (value v2) are Nodes; both children are leaves (each has both children Null, so the tree has exactly three nodes); v0, v1, and v2 are integers in [1, 10^6].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r is true, the root is a Node and its value is odd.
preconditions: root is not Null; the tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes; every node value is an integer in [1, 10^6].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r is true, every node at depth 1 (i.e., every child of the root) has an even value.
preconditions: root is not Null; the tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes; every node value is an integer in [1, 10^6].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r is true, if the root has both a left child and a right child, then the value of the left child is strictly greater than the value of the right child.
preconditions: root is not Null; the tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes; every node value is an integer in [1, 10^6].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r is true, every node at depth 2 has an odd value.
preconditions: root is not Null; the tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes; every node value is an integer in [1, 10^6].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r is true, the values of the nodes at depth 2, taken in left-to-right order, form a strictly increasing sequence (i.e., if v_0, v_1, ..., v_{k-1} are these values in left-to-right order, then v_0 < v_1 < ... < v_{k-1}).
preconditions: root is not Null; the tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes; every node value is an integer in [1, 10^6].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r is false.
preconditions: root is not Null; the tree has between 2 and 10^5 nodes; every node in the tree has the same integer value v, with v in [1, 10^6].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r is true.
preconditions: root is the binary tree whose level-order representation (including Null for missing children) is [1,10,4,3,null,7,9,12,8,6,null,null,2].

statement: The function returns a result r, and r is true if and only if for every node in the tree at depth d, its value is odd when d is even and even when d is odd.
preconditions: root is not Null; the tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes; every node in the tree has at most one child (i.e., for every Node, at least one of its children is Null); every node value is an integer in [1, 10^6].
